propositions: Four dispatch call sites use cast() to widen to optional capability types (SupportsComments, SupportsLinks) but perform no runtime guard, so a transport lacking the capability silently fails to apply the mutation inside a broad exception handler.
An AttributeError from a missing capability is indistinguishable from other exceptions and is swallowed, conflating designed skip (capability absent) with real failures, making the defect silent.

Call sites must be guarded with isinstance() checks against the @runtime_checkable capability Protocols before calling add_comment or set_relationship, and capability-absent must be logged and recorded distinctly in bridge_alerts with capability-specific alert kinds.
The isinstance guard must include a hasattr() fallback for compatibility across Python 3.11+ where @runtime_checkable behavior differs regarding proxied attributes served by __getattr__.

Capability present but raising must remain distinct from capability absent and continue to surface as a real failure in existing channels (warning, stderr, comment_errors) rather than as a capability-absent alert.
